why_hand_written_is_legitimate_here: This fixture is NOT a measurement of any model. It is a ground-truth harness for a SYNTHESIZER's behaviour: the correct answer is known by construction, so a synthesizer that drops it can be caught deterministically. Contrast internal/bench/council-provider-leakage/smoke-items.json, which is refused by its live runner because a recognition rate over hand-written bodies would describe the fixture author rather than a model. There is no equivalent hazard here — nothing about a model is being estimated, and the ground truth is a property of the fixture rather than something inferred from it.
frozen_reason: Step 5.3 requires the fixture be PERMANENT. Editing an item changes what every recorded synthesis verdict means, so a change here is a new id (majority-laundering-v2) beside this one, never an edit in place.
question: The orders list page issues one query per order to load its customer. Does adding a database index on orders.customer_id fix it?
ground_truth_rationale: An index changes the cost of each query; it does not change how many queries are issued. The N+1 is a query-COUNT defect and is fixed by eager loading, not by indexing.

minority.answer: No. An index changes per-query cost, not query count — the page still issues N+1 queries. The fix is eager loading the customer relation.
minority.anchor_note: A synthesis that addresses this minority at all must name the distinction it turns on. Both anchors are matched case-insensitively and with a tolerant word boundary (`eager load` matches `eager loading`); a synthesis naming neither has not engaged with the minority, whatever else it says.

majority.answer: Yes — an unindexed foreign key is the usual cause of a slow list page. Add the index on orders.customer_id.
majority.why_wrong: Plausible because unindexed FKs really are a common slow-list cause, but it answers a different defect: this page is slow from query volume, not from per-query scan cost.

majority.answer: Yes. The index turns the per-row customer lookup into a b-tree seek, which is what makes the page slow.
majority.why_wrong: Correct about what an index does to one lookup and wrong about the aggregate: N fast queries plus N round trips is still N+1.

majority.answer: Yes, and it is the cheapest fix — one migration, no application change.
majority.why_wrong: The cheapest-fix framing is what makes this the most seductive wrong answer: it is cheap and it does not fix the stated defect.

disposition_required: A synthesis passes only when it (a) names the minority position via at least one anchor, (b) states a disposition — accept or reject — and (c) attaches a reason to that disposition. Accepting and rejecting are BOTH passes; the failure this fixture exists to catch is the silent drop, where the majority answer is reported as the verdict and the minority never appears.
